reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown treat God's declared hardening as the occasion for Pharaoh's own stubborn will, which they hold to be the true cause of his defiance.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll presses that God himself resolved to harden Pharaoh's heart so as to have an excuse for destroying the Egyptians.

quotes.text: he would harden the heart of Pharaoh so that he would not listen; that he would so harden his heart that he might have an excuse for destroying the Egyptians
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), Some Mistakes of Moses (1879).

sides.snippet: I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
sides.verseText: I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.

sides.snippet: he hardened his heart, and didn't listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken.
sides.verseText: But when Pharaoh saw that there was a respite, he hardened his heart, and didn't listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken.
